evals.expected_output: Scopes via git log hot spots, explores with Explore sub-agents, then writes a self-contained HTML report of deepening candidates to the temp dir and asks which to explore.
expectations: Scopes the scan by walking recent git history (git log --oneline) to find hot spots, since no direction was given
Reads CONTEXT.md and ADRs before exploring, and plans to use Explore sub-agents to walk the codebase
Plans to write a self-contained HTML report to $TMPDIR (or /tmp) named architecture-review-<timestamp>.html and open it with xdg-open/open
Each candidate card includes Files, Problem, Solution, Benefits, a Before/After diagram, and a Strong / Worth exploring / Speculative badge, with a Top recommendation section
Does not propose interfaces yet and ends by asking 'Which of these would you like to explore?'

evals.prompt: /improve-codebase-architecture focus on the src/billing area — every change there touches like 6 files and the tests are all mocks.
evals.expected_output: Takes the named direction (src/billing) without git-log inference, applies the deletion test and deep-module vocabulary, and produces the HTML candidate report.
expectations: Takes src/billing as the scope and skips inferring hot spots from git history
Applies the deletion test to suspected shallow modules in billing
Uses codebase-design vocabulary (module, interface, depth, seam, adapter, leverage, locality) and avoids 'service', 'component', 'API' or 'boundary'
Frames benefits in terms of locality and leverage and how tests would improve (e.g. replacing mock-heavy tests with tests at the deepened interface)
Uses Tailwind and Mermaid via CDN for the HTML report with before/after diagrams per candidate

evals.prompt: /improve-codebase-architecture — note we have docs/adr/0004-separate-read-and-write-models.md, please respect it. Mainly worried about the order intake code.
evals.expected_output: Scopes to order intake, respects ADR-0004 and only surfaces conflicting candidates with a clear warning callout, then moves to a grilling loop with domain-modeling side effects once a candidate is picked.
expectations: Reads ADR-0004 and does not re-litigate it, only surfacing a conflicting candidate with an explicit 'contradicts ADR-0004 — but worth reopening because…' style callout
Names modules using CONTEXT.md domain vocabulary (e.g. 'the Order intake module') rather than class names or 'service'
Describes that after the user picks a candidate it will run a /grilling loop through constraints, seam placement and surviving tests
Mentions offering an ADR if the user rejects a candidate for a load-bearing reason, so future reviews don't re-suggest it
